classification: Designed product visualizations, not live screenshots.

assets.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a high-fidelity designed product visualization of the actual TrendInk creative studio for its founder's portfolio. Wide landscape 16:9, approximately 2048x1152. Perfectly front-facing orthographic application screen filling the entire image, no device, no browser chrome, no surrounding frame, no perspective, no marketing headline, no watermark. Apply the authentic brand: small exact silver photographic aperture icon with red-orange center from reference at top left, then the exact wordmark "TrendInk" in white Manrope bold. Never invent or simplify its logo. Interface font Manrope with crisp legible sentence-case labels and carefully spaced clean typography. Surface palette deep graphite #0d1116 and #161b22, thin subtle silver separators, clear ivory type, muted gray secondary text, controlled red-orange #ff6254 selection and action accents. Sophisticated editorial production software, not a generic business dashboard. Large deliberate image areas, restrained controls, no fake analytics or performance scores, no platform logos, no card-count statistics. Use real concise readable text, no pseudo-text, no lorem ipsum. This is a designed visualization grounded in the app workflow: Signal, Direction, Story, Scenes, Produce, Edit, Export. Reference 1 is the existing TrendInk Story Studio visualization for cinematic art/style inspiration; reference 2 is the exact genuine aperture branding. Make a beautifully composed STORY STUDIO scene-planning view with a cinematic noir project called "After the rain". Top header "TrendInk" then "After the rain" with controls "Save draft" and an orange "Approve story" button. Horizontal stage navigation directly below: "Signal", "Direction", "Story" (active), "Scenes", "Produce", "Edit", "Export". Main content has a narrow 18% editorial column at left headed "Story treatment" containing three clear fields: "Opening hook" with "A city changes when the rain stops.", "Point of view" with "Find the human story in ordinary streets.", "Source thread" with "Street footage" and a small linked-reference icon, then an understated "Direction approved" text status. Remaining main area is an expansive board of SIX cinematic storyboard images in two rows of three, with excellent proportion and almost all image. Black-and-white cinematic photography of same dark-haired male protagonist with black coat, night city, wet streets, real film grain, deep silver blacks and beautiful reflected light. Respect the noir visual story of the reference but improve the image direction: 1 a wide rain-soaked empty street and lone figure; 2 close-up of his expressive face beside rain-speckled window; 3 a long black car under city streetlights; 4 same man looking over a glowing city rooftop; 5 same man entering a narrow wet alley; 6 close-up of hand holding a small worn silver keepsake. Fine orange border on Scene 04. Under each cinematic image use only clean concise two-line caption: "01 · Opening" / "The city waits", "02 · Character" / "A private moment", "03 · Movement" / "Through the streets", "04 · Turning point" / "Above the city", "05 · Pursuit" / "One more block", "06 · Resolution" / "What remains". At bottom a narrow inspector strip for selected scene: "Scene 04" "Wide shot" "Slow push in" "Night exterior" "Source linked". Make the cinematic story imagery prominent and compelling while the header and controls remain confidently readable. All layout fits the screen without crop or scrollbar. No badge clutter, no neon gradients, no decorative glow.
